[TaurusHead] I sort of agree with that but for gaming (CS), Windows seems to be the most compatible OS
[Zythyx] @TaurusHead: It's a very different landscape these days. While there are still games that will not work because of Anti-cheat (like Fortnite, Valorant, Apex or LoL), with translation layers and games being available natively for Linux, it's easier than ever to get into Linux as a gamer - thank SteamOS and Proton for that.
2 months ago I tried a dual-boot setup for Windows and CachyOS (Arch Distro) and I've only once booted into Windows because I messed up the boot sequence. The only reason I haven't completely blown away my Windows installation is because I rarely play Fortnite with friends, so I need it available. Everything else has been smooth as butter - WoW, Final Fantasy VII/XIV, Palworld, Satisfactory are all games I've played so far.
Counterstrike seems to work great on CachyOS too, but I haven't yet tried it
See https://wiki.cachyos.org/configuration/gaming/ for more gaming details

Just wipe it and move on.
[trippy] What's the Ryzen R2544 like? Would it run retrogames with emulators?
[SpiffyTheDog] Depends what retro games you're planning, but generally anything up to PS2 would be a doddle
[tonyjzx] https://www.techpowerup.com/cpu-specs/ryzen-embedded-r2544.c…
i'm of the opinion these are veering towards e-waste given they are Zen + and in 2026 that's getting kinda old
the architecture predates the ps5 and that's already ancient shit
BUT you get fuc all for $300 these days and so performance should be ok
https://www.cpubenchmark.net/cpu.php?cpu=AMD+Ryzen+Embedded+…
the thing benches a bit better than an N150
but these seem to be designed for thin clients so… yeah…. would people say sub R3 3100?
if you wanna troll around ebay you get the occasional $300 lenovo m910 or whatever than runs an i5-10400t whatever and i think that would be a better buy??? esp. if you can find one that takes a slimline vga
[blahman] For better bang for buck probably get one it those used b grade laptops and use them as minipc.
[Frackingiscool] As long as you are realistic, yes.
If you got the 16gb ram you could dedicate 2gb to the igpu and vega 8 should comfortably handle PS2 and lower on batocera/CachyOS/etc
[DisasterArea] I've got a slower N97 unit that plays batocera like a god. hundreds of old video arcade roms FTW.
[SS625] Can I turn this into a truenas? How many sata slot on the mb?
[jaybo] 2x m.2 slots, one is PCIE and the other is sata only.
you should be fine to run truenas, but hwo many drives do you want and how much do you want to hack up the case to route sata cables if the answer to "how many drives do you want to run" is "more than 2x m.2 sata drives"?
[Tiggrrrrr] Sorry if its a stupid question, but I haven't used a desktop in years, and never one of these mini desktops.
Are these good for basic office tasks?
e.g. Excel (mainly for data analysis), powerpoint, MS Project, web page development.
[despavr] It has plenty of RAM for those activities, it may struggle if you try to do stuff like watching 4k videos etc.
But for those basic office applicatios, $300 for a PC is a good buy

[Esteban5150] For a JellyFin server, this or a HP Elitedesk 800 G2 mini with Intel i5-6500T 2.50Ghz 16Gb RAM
[ozbargainhunter400] Neither. 6500T is old AF. You need 11th gen intel, the GPU with that will do everything.
Intel over the AMD though for jellyfin if you can’t afford anything else.
[lachlantula] this is a bit harsh i reckon. my 7500t, which is basically the same cpu - thank you 14nm++++ era - works just great for this very purpose imo. intel quicksync is well supported by jellyfin.
only issue is if you want to decode 10-bit hevc really
having said that would i pick the 6500t system over this mini pc? yeah probably not. video transcoding might be worse on vega - im not entirely sure - but the raw grunt of the ryzen chip will be very handy
[homebrandjesus] N150 > either option for Plex or jellyfin.
[Roe Jogan] what's the reliability and power consumption for like a hermes setup? i mean i do have a intel nuc laptop but wonder if that's dangerous for continues running due to battery
[bonechiller] This should be plenty for hermes. But I am assuming you are using cloud ai providers as this will struggle with local models.
I have hermes running in a VM and it doesn’t need too much resource allocation as long as the models are running in the cloud.
This should be alright for basic hermes desktop usage as well.

[batrarobin] Thank you, yes that's the plan, have a few other services like Plex etc to run on the same machine.
[bamzero] Drop Proxmox on it and checkout the helper scripts and you'll start finding all sorts of things to run that you hadn't thought of.
[batrarobin] @bamzero: Thanks, yeah have heard a lot about Proxmox here on OzB and have been meaning to try out.
[bamzero] Only if you've already got a Pi lying around of course, not worth buying a new one these days.
[boomramada] For HA, even PI is cheap; use this. HA does a lot of read/write, which corrupts your SD card in no time unless you boot up with an external drive, which is costly these days.
